owner: W1-POPULATION — the hostile population of the province
source: RI-AI07 §D (density budget), RI-AI05 §C/§D (composition, the introduction rule, the legal pairings), RI-WLD02 D9/D10 (hostile groups per minute), RI-PRG06 §7 (the ≈1,230 census), ARBITRATION S5 (respawn), S9 (no level scaling), S17 (2.0 m·s⁻¹).
_why_this_file_exists: Before it, the entire hostile population of Black Marsh was two rows in encounters.json with no coordinates — nine bodies, one statblock, worth 1,224 souls between them, which is level 3 against a plan of level 82. Placement lived in hand-written state files: `applyNamedState` spawned `patch.encounters` and nothing else, so the world was exactly as populated as somebody had remembered to type. This file is the MODEL — density, falloff and composition — and it is read at runtime by `game/src/world/population.js`, not merely by the generator. Perturb a number here and bodies appear, disappear or change archetype on the next walk; `tools/world/population-consumption.mjs` does exactly that.

budget._speed_note: ARBITRATION S17 / RI-WLD01. A traversal minute is 120 m, which is why RI-AI07 §D's per-TM figures and RI-WLD02 D9's per-minute figures are the same density in two units.
budget._grouped_size_derivation: 0.55×1 + 0.45×G = 1.9 ⇒ G = 3.0. Grouped encounters must average three bodies. Every tier's composition table below is weighted to hit that, and build-population.mjs reports the realised mean per tier so the claim is checkable rather than asserted.

tier_multiplier._note: RI-AI07 §D region modifiers, applied to enemies-per-TM. Tier 5 returning to baseline is deliberate and is RI-AI05's whole thesis: late difficulty comes from which questions are asked at once, not from more bodies. `danger_tier` is already declared per region in game/data/world/regions.json and this is the first thing in the build that consumes it for anything.

safety._model: Density is zero on top of a place of safety and ramps to full over `ramp_m`. This is the second axis the brief asks for — distance from safety, not only region tier — and it is what makes a road out of a town legible: you get a hundred metres to look at the country before the country looks back.
safety._ramp_note: Linear from 0 at `clear_m` to 1.0 at `clear_m + ramp_m`. At a settlement that puts the first encounter roughly 90–170 m out — inside RI-AI07 §D's ≤1.70 TM (204 m) longest-zero-enemy stretch, which a bigger clear radius would breach.
safety._hearth_apron_note: A HEARTH IS A CHECKPOINT, NOT A SAFE ZONE, and getting that wrong is what the first run of the generator did: at a 45 m clear and a 150 m ramp the thirteen critical-path hearths strung along the crossing suppressed 390 m out of every 500 m of it, and the road that the whole game is about came out at 0.43 encounters per traversal minute against a floor of 0.59. In a Souls game an enemy stands twenty metres from the bonfire, in sight of it, and that is the point: the apron is 22 m and full density is back by 62 m. RI-PRG04's only protected corridor is the one from a fog-gate hearth to its gate, and that has its own rule below.
safety._deep_note: Beyond `deep_bonus_at_m` from any safety the multiplier rises to `deep_bonus` — a mild 15%, because RI-WLD02 D9's ceiling is 1.2 groups/min and the tier multiplier already spends most of the headroom. Going off the road is supposed to feel less safe; it is not supposed to be a different game.
safety._fog_gate_note: RI-PRG04 §5 / RI-AI06: the hearth serving a fog gate must be 60–110 s from it with NO respawning enemy in between. 110 s at 2.0 m·s⁻¹ is 220 m; the two shipped corridors are 84 s and shorter. No post is generated inside a capsule of this radius around the segment from a fog-gate hearth to its gate.

road_corridor._model: Encounters are placed ALONG the trunk road, offset to one side, because RI-AI07 §B's sightline rule is about the player's approach and the road is the approach. Offsets alternate sides deterministically.
road_corridor._separation_note: RI-AI07 §B SL8 wants ≥18 m between encounter VOLUMES. A volume here is at most ~5 m of members plus the rule's 6 m skirt, so 26 m between post centres clears 18 m between volumes with margin.

poi_garrison._model: A ruin is not a road. RI-WLD02 D10 puts a Souls-loop dungeon at 2.0–3.5 hostile groups per minute — roughly triple the road — and the ten `landmark` POIs are the exterior end of that. Each landmark that is not a fog gate gets a garrison ring: posts on a circle around it, at the region's own tier.
poi_garrison._skip_note: the-drowned-xanmeer and ceyatatar-zel-ayleid-vault ARE the two fog gates. Their bosses are content behind a gate; a garrison outside them would sit inside the fog-gate corridor above and would be farmed from the hearth.

composition._model: The lever RI-AI05 §D ranks first and second — a new archetype, then a new COMBINATION of existing archetypes — and never levers 5–8 (more damage, more HP, faster attacks, level scaling). Every weight below selects a TEMPLATE from game/data/world/encounters.json; no template changes a stat. Weights are per danger_tier and sum to 1.0.

introduction_rule._rule: RI-AI05 §D, and it is a hard fail there rather than a preference: the first instance of any archetype in the game must be presented SOLO, in a lit, open, non-ambush position, with retreat available. The generator walks the province in canonical order — the crossing first, then the remaining legs, then the garrisons — and the first post that would introduce a statblock the player has not met is replaced by that statblock's solo template. The order it produces is written into population-posts.json as `introduction_order` so a critic can read it without re-running the build.

stream._model: THE WORLD-SIDE CONSUMER. `game/src/world/population.js` holds every post in a coarse grid and is pumped from `Engine._streamPopulation()`, which runs from `Engine._afterStep()` beside `_streamProvince()` — the one slot every way the world advances passes through (stepFrames, the rAF accumulator, walkRoute, walkPath, travelRide). A post within `spawn_radius_m` of the player becomes bodies; beyond `release_radius_m` its living bodies are removed again. Nothing here slows the player down (S17) and nothing reads player level (S9).
stream._hysteresis_note: 90 m of hysteresis between the two, for the reason the province streamer needed one tile of it: a body standing on the boundary otherwise spawns and releases on alternate frames. 170 m also sits comfortably outside the widest aggro radius in the roster (20 m) and outside RI-AI07 §B SL2's 12 m sightline floor, so nothing is ever born inside its own aggro range.
stream._refocus_note: The candidate set is only recomputed after the player has moved this far. At 2.0 m·s⁻¹ that is once per 4 s of walking.
stream._budget_note: One post materialises per fixed step at most. A four-body post costs four `engine.spawn()` calls, each of which builds a combat body and evaluates a rig, so they are spread exactly as the province streamer spreads tile builds.

respawn._binding: ARBITRATION S5, and game/data/world/respawn.json is the authority — this file adds nothing to it and takes nothing away. A post that has been cleared stays cleared until an ordinary respawn happens; on a hearth rest or a player death, DeathSystem.respawnOrdinary() revives every resident ordinary body AND bumps `ordinaryRespawnEpoch`, which is what tells the population system that cleared posts far from the player may stand up again.
respawn.never_respawns: Nothing in this file can respawn a named NPC, a merchant, a trainer, a quest actor or a boss. Those live in `sim.npcs` (a different array, which no code path here iterates) or carry a never-respawn flag that `DeathSystem.respawns()` already refuses. The population system spawns ONLY through `Engine.spawnEncounter()` → `Engine.spawn()`, so `_classifyOnSpawn` runs on every body it makes and the existing classification is what decides.

declared_incomplete.interiors: RI-WLD07 §2–3 wants ≈849 hostiles inside 8 Souls-loop dungeons and 82 Morrowind interiors. This file places the EXTERIOR population only — trunk-road corridor and landmark garrisons. Interiors are 115 files in game/data/world/interiors/ and are a separate placement problem with a separate density bar (RI-WLD02 D10, 2.0–3.5 groups/min). Not attempted, not faked, not counted.
declared_incomplete.archetypes: See encounters.json `absent_roles_declared`. Five of RI-AI05's ten roles have no shipped statblock, so the mix is INFANTRY/BEAST only.
declared_incomplete.ambushes: RI-AI07 §C's fair-ambush rule needs an AMBUSHER statblock and an authored environmental cue per position. Neither exists. No post in this build is an ambush, which is legal (AM1 is a ceiling, not a floor) and is why `ambushes per loop` reads 0.
